name: l2-peak
rationale: Base (chain 8453), the highest block rate any supported chain presents. 2s blocks means 0.5 blocks/s on chain; this offers 10.0 blocks/s, 20x that, on the same burst reasoning as mainnet-peak. Base blocks are smaller and more frequent, so 120 tx/block gives 1200 declared tps -- the highest chain rate in the fleet, and where the block-rate side of the fast path breaks first if it breaks at all. Alerting fraction 1.0, as in mainnet-peak. The API mix is held identical on purpose: the API does not care which chain produced the load, and holding it constant is what makes the two profiles' API numbers comparable. The screening route is driven as a POST because that is what it is (§11 -- a screening decision is a billable, audited event, not a cacheable read); a GET-only driver would collect 405s in microseconds and report the route as the fastest thing in the system.
